## Constructing a straight line {#fv3-construct .fv-lesson .line-lesson}

```{=html}
<p>How could we construct <span data-math="\underset{\sim}{r}"></span> so that its tip traces a line through <span data-math="A"></span>?</p><div data-line-construction></div>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet §§3.1–3.2 · pp. 36–38</div>

::: {.notes}
Begin with the fixed position vector OA and a non-zero vector d parallel to the line. Ask how to construct r before moving the slider. Show r=OA+λd as one vector sum. Adjust λ to move the tip of r along the line, while OA stays fixed. At λ=0 the tip is A; positive and negative values reach both sides of A. The same equation describes the entire line as λ ranges over all real numbers. The slider samples −1≤λ≤2; its range is not the domain of the line. The points and arrows share exact coordinates. Connect the equation to the opening example x=3−t, y=2t. No construction-step sequence is used.
:::
